findings.claim: The eCornell URL in References breaks across a line as "business-s" / "trategy/."
findings.source: Rendered page, and the raw PDF text layer.
findings.reason: The template's xurl package deliberately allows a URL to break at any character so long URLs never overflow the margin, and inserts no character at the break. Verified independently by extracting the raw PDF text layer at that spot: it reads exactly "business-s\ntrategy/." with no inserted hyphen glyph -- the only "-" present is the genuine one in "business-strategy," so the URL copies and concatenates correctly; the break only looks like a hyphenated word split.
findings.verification: Declined by the coordinator (xurl allows arbitrary URL breaks to avoid margin overflow; no character is inserted). Confirmed independently in the prior pass by reading the raw PDF text layer at that spot. Unchanged in this edition; decline stands.

findings.claim: "Disintermediation"'s glossary definition included a clause ("or being cut out itself") not taught anywhere in chapter 6's body.
findings.source: Chapter 6, section 6.6: "Disintermediation or competition: the platform may copy successful products or steer customers to its own" -- describes only the platform cutting out the seller.
findings.fix: Reword the entry to match what 6.6 actually teaches.
findings.verification: Now reads: "Disintermediation. A platform cutting out the businesses that sell through it, for example by selling its own version of their products. [6]" -- matches 6.6's "the platform may copy successful products or steer customers to its own" exactly, with no unsupported second clause.

findings.claim: "Winner-take-all" had a glossary entry but was never used or explained in chapter 6's body prose, and its definition was circular with "tipping."
findings.source: Text search found "winner-take-all" only in 6.9 (Key terms) and its own glossary entry; 6.4's discussion of tipping never used the term.
findings.fix: Introduce the term where the concept is taught, and give it a non-circular definition distinct from "tipping."
findings.verification: 6.4 now reads: "...push a market toward one winner (a winner-take-all market); the opposite conditions allow more than one platform to survive" -- the term is introduced (bolded, matching the book's treatment of other first-defined terms like envelopment) exactly where the concept is taught. The glossary entry is now non-circular: "A market in which one platform ends up with most of the users and most of the value," clearly distinct from "Tipping. A market moving toward one dominant platform" (tipping = the process, winner-take-all = the resulting state). Confirmed on the rendered page 42 -- clean layout, no overflow from the insertion.

findings.claim: Four terms named in 6.9's Key terms (price structure, subsidy side, seeding, platform governance) were still missing from the glossary.
findings.source: 6.9: "Platform; two-sided market; price structure; subsidy side." / "Chicken-and-egg problem; seeding; single-side value." / "Envelopment; platform governance."
findings.fix: Add glossary entries for these four, tagged [6].
findings.verification: All four added and checked against their basis in the body: "Platform governance" ("The rules a platform sets and enforces for its participants, which decide whether they trust it") matches 6.5's "govern the platform so participants trust it"; "Price structure" ("How a platform splits its total charges between its sides") matches 6.3's "the structure of prices matters... how the total charge is split between the sides"; "Seeding" ("Bringing one side of a platform yourself, such as signing suppliers before buyers arrive") matches 6.5's "bring one side yourself (seed supply)" and is consistent with the worked example's "FieldTable signed 20 farms first"; "Subsidy side" ("The side of a platform that pays little or nothing, because the other side values its presence") matches 6.3's subsidize-the-side rule. Alphabetical order re-checked and still holds with all four insertions (confirmed on rendered pages 53-56). No new issues found.
